The built-in GDEVELOP_OPENAI_TOOLS schema is ~6.5k tokens of serialized JSON (measure it on JSON.stringify, not the indented source — the source reads ~10.8k and overstates by 65%). It shares the request's context window with the messages, so any budget that only measures messages over-sends on small local models.

When subtracting a large fixed cost from a budget, clamp with a floor: without one, a model whose window cannot hold the fixed cost gets a zero budget and silently loses its system prompt and history — a worse failure than the oversized request it was meant to prevent.

Measured tool-budget outcome (verified): tools ~6524 tokens. llama window 8192 -> messages 4096 before / 1024 after, total 7548 which now FITS (before: 10620, over). qwen-mistral 32768 -> 16384 before / 9860 after, total exactly 16384. gpt/claude/deepseek 128000 -> 64000 / 57476. So the floor does not merely avoid silent amnesia on llama: it makes the request fit. The commit message's claim that the shortfall 'surfaces through the server's context-length error' applies only to a hypothetical model whose window is below ~7.6k, not to llama.

Budget what you send, not what you built: the compaction measured the head template while the JSON instruction tail was appended after measurement - always measure the exact messages array the request sends (measurePrompt over system+user), the same way trimMessagesToBudget measures what it trims.

Chrome DevTools MCP via code mode: the runtime has no setTimeout (use wait_for or the tool's own waits), and evaluate_script requires a function-declaration string (e.g. '() => {...}'), not an IIFE - an invoked string returns a value and fails with 'fn is not a function'.

A local OpenAI-compatible server's CORS preflight only allows a fixed header set; sending optional attribution headers (HTTP-Referer/X-Title) blocks the whole request in the browser build before it reaches the model. Keep the outbound header set minimal (Content-Type) for local-first, and verify new headers against a real Ollama preflight, not just axios mocks - mocks do not model CORS.

Driving the Ask AI new-chat form via Chrome DevTools MCP is unreliable here: the drawer re-renders back to the history list between fill and send. For the multi-turn benchmark, use the @feedback-loop skill / interactive session rather than synthetic DOM driving; a single-turn live BYOK check is enough to validate the transport.

Ollama's OpenAI-compatible SSE sends `delta.reasoning` (not `reasoning_content`) and streams it for many chunks before any `delta.content`; any UI signal derived from partial content (the cold-start hint, the streaming tail) must account for reasoning-only progress or it reports 'waiting for the first token' while the model is clearly working.

Telemetry the console already prints should also be stored in a registry keyed by request id: 'inspectable' in this objective means readable from React state, not just visible in devtools. Thread a callback (onProviderTelemetry) through the client like onStreamDelta rather than having the client guess the request id.

Auditing revertibility with `git show <sha> | git apply --reverse --check` is wrong for a commit older than HEAD: git apply checks against the working tree, so any later commit touching the same lines makes it conflict regardless of true revertibility. Verify with `git revert --no-commit` on the tip or a newest-first range instead, and confirm the history is linear (no merges) first.

Driving a React controlled input via Chrome DevTools: fill() sets the DOM value but does not fire the input event React listens for (the send button stays disabled); use click to focus then press_key/type_text so real key events update state. This is why earlier new-chat sends failed intermittently.

A find-based python splice is unsafe when the same anchor text appears in more than one turn path (three near-identical send blocks here): the restore matched the wrong occurrence and spliced a function body into another. After such an edit, run eslint immediately; if it reports variables 'not defined' in a region you did not touch, the splice is wrong - revert the file to HEAD and re-apply each edit with its own unique anchor + lint check.

A browser client can only read custom response headers from a cross-origin endpoint if the server lists them in Access-Control-Expose-Headers; a proxy advertising x-omniroute-* must expose them or the telemetry is invisible to the editor (proven live in cycle 202).

Invariant-2 OSINT must be a real assessment, not a reflex swap: ajv is the maintained validator, but adopting it as a direct dependency for a hot-path per-tool-call check in the editor bundle costs more than the small, schema-driven, test-pinned bespoke validator it would replace. Record the reasoning so it is not re-opened each session.

In this build the standalone Ask AI form does not host a project for the editor function map, so project-requiring tools (create_or_update_plan, create_scene, ...) fail there even after initialize_project creates one; the editor container with a project open is required for those. initialize_project itself works standalone (EditorFunctionWithoutProject).

Deterministic harness > model: scripted MOCK_SCRIPT turns exposed a studio defect (plan never flips to done) that model-dependent runs had hidden as 'model variance'. The write gate only serializes gated writes; the model turn writes the cache directly, so a gated write can still be clobbered by a turn's snapshot-based write.

JSX splits a literal adjacent to an expression across lines into words: `<Trans>{n} sub-agent{n===1?'':'s'}</Trans>` rendered 'sub-agent s'. Build such a sentence as a single interpolated string, not adjacent text/expression nodes.
Adding a field to a summarizer's return breaks exact-equality tests: update the callers' expectations (here three tests) in the same change, or the suite goes red for a correct improvement.

loadLocalAiRequests MERGES persisted entries into the in-memory cache and never clears it, so a test asserting on its return value can pass/fail on in-memory state rather than what was persisted - assert on the storage JSON when testing persistence.

Run scripts/check-fork-divergence.js BEFORE committing any edit to a file you have not confirmed is in the manifest: a correct fix in an upstream-identical file still creates new divergence (two paths here), and the policy is to revert it when production reachability is theoretical and the fix belongs upstream.

The client normalizes a non-Error rejection to a generic 'AI request failed' Error (cycle 172), which drops axios-style `.code` - so any error-CLASSIFYING predicate (network vs provider) must be fed an Error instance in tests, and must not rely on `.code` for a non-Error rejection (message patterns are the fallback).

When a defensive helper is extracted (cycle 160's parentHasOutputForCall), grep for DUPLICATED copies of the same check: AiRequestContext's watch loop kept its own unguarded version for 74 cycles. Extraction only closes the class if every copy is routed through it.

A recorded-but-unsent result is a loop: when a branch records an outcome with addEditorFunctionCallResults but the batch has no editor calls, it must also SEND it via onSendEditorFunctionCallResults, or the model never advances and the batch reprocesses until the loop guard trips. The harness caught this only through a role-denied-only batch (a case no spec covered).
